### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 062a2323ba363d15f507433987cca4d650979b40`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **32** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 062a2323ba363d15f507433987cca4d650979b40` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eb28a88492c50d939abd7af927ca7ab00b978620` — the merge of head `dbc6f440b9aaf1b38d1d6c39442dbae91fd73683` into base `062a2323ba363d15f507433987cca4d650979b40`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eb28a88492c50d939abd7af927ca7ab00b978620 && git checkout eb28a88492c50d939abd7af927ca7ab00b978620
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 062a2323ba363d15f507433987cca4d650979b40 dbc6f440b9aaf1b38d1d6c39442dbae91fd73683 && git checkout -B drift-repro 062a2323ba363d15f507433987cca4d650979b40 && git merge --no-ff dbc6f440b9aaf1b38d1d6c39442dbae91fd73683

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 062a2323ba363d15f507433987cca4d650979b40
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 062a2323ba363d15f507433987cca4d650979b40` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9ae8fc1682699ce3aeef51ebd726cb4151070018`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/declared-datasources.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/code-datasource-names.ts, packages/runtime/src/index.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/declared-datasources.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/install-local-declared-datasources.dogfood.test.ts + packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-connection-service.ts (`connectDeclared`, `disconnect`, `getConnectionState`), packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts (`createDatasource`), packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts (`putDatasourceRecord`, boot restore), packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts (`get`, `unregister`, `registerInMemory`), packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts (`runtime.package-jobs` cleanup shape), packages/cli/src/commands/package/install.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/marketplaceApi.ts, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Declaration at this head: the changeset `.changeset/28039-install-local-declared-datasources.md` declares `fix(cloud-connection)!:`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a BREAKING banner and `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. That is the declaration this review judges. The PR body's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line and the title without `!` are SUPERSEDED by the changeset: this PR widens (new `@objectstack/runtime` export `connectPackageDatasources` + 4 types; new optional `datasources` member on the install-local answer) AND narrows (a package declaring a datasource name the environment already holds is refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `details.datasource`, where `main` answered `200`). The relay cannot edit the body; the corrected reading is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, BREAKING, `!`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Widening 1 — `connectPackageDatasources` + `DeclaredDatasourceOwner`, `OwnedDatasources`, `PackageDatasourceOptions`, `PackageDatasourceVerdict` exported from `@objectstack/runtime`** (`index.ts`). Correct: `@objectstack/cloud-connection` resolves it by `await import('@objectstack/runtime')` with a logged fallback when the runtime predates it, so a package-level export is required; it cannot stay module-internal. `withdrawCodeDatasourceNames` and `CodeDatasourceNames.delete` stay unexported from the package, as the body says. Judged right.
- **Widening 2 — install-local answer gains `datasources: [{ name, status }]`**, omitted (not emptied) when the package declares none, so the answer's key set for every existing caller is unchanged (same shape as `credentialRefs`, #27237). `status` values are the connection service's existing `ConnectStatus` names, no new vocabulary. Judged right.
- **Narrowing — step 2a `findHeldDatasourceName`**: literal `default` → refused; else `metadata.get('datasource', name)` with `_packageId !== manifestId` → refused. Covers the host's `default`, the boot artifact's (in-memory, stamped), Setup-created (`putDatasourceRecord` → `metadata.register('datasource', …)` at create, and re-registered at boot restore, `origin: 'runtime'`) and another installed package's (registered in memory by the helper). Placed after the `user-code` MANIFEST_CONFLICT check and before step 2b, which the existing code pins as "BEFORE hot-register and before anything is written to the ledger"; nothing is written before it. A reinstall/upgrade of the SAME package passes (`owner === manifestId` skips); the `kernel:ready` rehydrate does not run 2a at all, so a restart never refuses a ledgered package. Judged right; two fail-open edges noted in ③.
- **Boot path (Q1)**: `AppPlugin.start` is behaviour-identical for consumers. Registration + connect now run through the helper with `installed` unset: no withdraw, no name contribution (phase-1 contribution at `app-plugin.ts:626` is untouched), ownership stamping via `owned: () => this.codeDefinedDatasourceOwners(ctx)` resolved inside the same lenient `warn` catch as before, the same `datasources` list by reference (#23029), the same three log lines, and the fail-fast verdict re-thrown so boot is refused. Differences, none contractual: `registerDeclaredApiEndpoints` now runs after the connect instead of between registration and connect (it reads `definition.apis` only); the datasource collection is converted once instead of twice; a throw from `convertedCollection`/`resolveMappedObjects` itself now propagates without the `[AppPlugin] declared-datasource auto-connect failed` log line (it still refuses boot).
- **Held-name check completeness (Q2)**: complete for every holder the metadata service knows. Not seen: a driver registered only on the engine with no metadata registration (the legacy `onEnable` escape hatch) — the install then proceeds and the verdict surfaces as `already-registered` in `datasources`, not silently. Acceptable; noted in ③.
- **Uninstall/reinstall (Q3)**: `withdrawPackageDatasources` calls `connection.disconnect(name)` (closes the pool, drops the retained verdict, clears the engine's unavailable mark, evicts the driver — `datasource-connection-service.ts`), unregisters the metadata item only when still stamped with this package, withdraws the names from the set and clears the WeakMap entry. The cleanup is registered once per protocol under `runtime.package-datasources` on the same `registerUninstallCleanup` registry `runtime.package-jobs` uses, so both the install-local `DELETE` and the protocol's `deletePackage` run it. `INSTALLED_BY_APP` is a WeakMap keyed by the kernel's `CodeDatasourceNames` instance (created before `kernelKey` is read), `DATASOURCE_CLEANUP_REGISTERED` a WeakSet keyed by the protocol: no cross-kernel leak. A reinstall withdraws first (unit test pins `[STORE, VAULT]` → `[STORE]`). Judged right.
- **Unresolved credential**: `connectDeclared` attempts every datasource, then throws (`fatal` aggregation); the helper on `installed` logs, reads back each retained verdict via `getConnectionState` and returns it; install still answers `200`; bound read `503 ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` (dogfood). The diff does not decide where a code datasource's credential comes from: it hands `external.credentialsRef` to the connection service's existing resolver (#27687 untouched, stated in the module header and the PR). Judged right.
- **Tests**: unit file pins the installed/boot split (names recorded or not, thrown vs reported, reinstall withdrawal, cleanup scoped to the package and to registrations still stamped with it, no connection service). Dogfood pins both verdicts on the answer, `origin: 'code'` + `_packageId/_packageVersion`, code-set membership, admin list `ok`/`error`, write+read through the driver, `503`, uninstall `cleanups` entry `{ success: true, removed: 2 }`, 409 for `showcase_external` and `default` with nothing reaching the set or the connection service, and the rehydrate after restart. Adequate for the acceptance scenario.

### ② Semver level

- Both entries `patch` with a BREAKING banner and `!` under `Metadata-protocol: none`: correct per `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` LEVEL AXIS (ruling A): the level is decided only by the `Metadata-protocol:` kind; a non-protocol narrowing "ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition". No authorable key, value, default or type moves here.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is a recognised spelling (`clause2-line.mjs:113`: widens one surface and narrows another) and is the true one: the arm is what the ADR-0087 gate and the queue guard read.
- `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: justified. No spec key, Zod schema, stored shape or exported declaration is removed or narrowed (only added); nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite; the changeset body carries no FROM→TO rewrite or migration table (the "remedy" sentence is a naming choice, not a prescription), so the category's one mechanical refusal does not fire.
- Changeset prose checked against the diff: "Before/Now/Unchanged/Who sees it", "one path", "install answer carries `datasources` … omitted for a package that declares none", "credential that cannot be resolved … named non-`ok` verdict … 503", "reinstall replaces … uninstall closes pools, removes registrations and names, reported as `runtime.package-datasources` in `cleanups`" — all true. One overstatement: "the ADR-0062 D2 gate … apply as on a boot" — D2 (d) (`datasourceMapping` routing) never fires for an installed package because install-local passes no `mappedObjects` (the PR body says so); the gate's (a)(b)(c) legs apply as on a boot.
- Docs callout (`external-datasources.mdx`): every sentence true against the diff (registered `origin: code`, read-only, auto-connected at install and every restart, failed `status` kept, `503 ERR_DATASOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`, `datasources` on the answer, `409` on a held name).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Declaration mismatch (process, not code)**: the PR body's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and the `!`-less title are superseded by the changeset's `yes (narrowing)` / `fix(...)!:` / BREAKING. Consequences for the dispatcher: the PR's "Dogfood battery: n/a (no `!`, no `(narrowing)` arm)" line was written under the stale declaration; whatever the battery owes a `!`/narrowing PR is owed here, and the ADR-0087 gate reads the arm from the body on the next `edited` event.
- **#27687 not decided by this diff**: confirmed. The helper resolves nothing itself; the installed datasources now reach the connection service's one resolver and `CODE_DATASOURCE_NAMES_SERVICE.has(name)`, so whatever #27687 rules reaches them.
- **Fail-open edges in 2a** (not must-fix, name them for a follow-up card): (i) a `metadata.get` that throws, or a kernel with no `metadata` service, `continue`s/returns `undefined` → the install proceeds; the in-memory registry answers first, so every holder this PR names is seen without a loader, but a loader-only holder behind an outage is not. (ii) A holder registered on the engine only (legacy `onEnable` bridge) is not seen; the answer then carries `already-registered`, visibly.
- **Pre-existing collision after upgrade**: a Setup-created row with the same name as a datasource of a package installed on `main` before this PR (allowed then, since the name was not code) is not refused at the restart's rehydrate (2a is install-only): `registerInMemory` overwrites the in-memory item, `connectDeclared` answers `already-registered` from the Setup pool, and the name joins the code set (the row turns read-only in Setup; a later uninstall's `disconnect` would evict that pool). Rare, documented remedy exists (rename), worth one sentence in the changeset or a follow-up; not a must-fix.
- **D2 (d) for installed packages**: `datasourceMapping` rules are not installed by this door before or after, so a datasource reachable only through a mapping rule stays unconnected for an installed package. Stated in the PR; unchanged behaviour.
- **Out-of-scope finding the PR reports**: the `503` text claims "failed to connect at startup … OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE" for an install-time failure (`packages/objectql/src/driver-connect-errors.ts`) — carded by the seat as #28135.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no extra login note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Narrowing against the published spec on `main`**: install-local's accept set on `main` admitted a package whose declared datasource name was already held and silently dropped the declaration (`200`, `hotLoaded: true`, objects `404`). With the datasources now registered as code and connected, admitting such a package would serve its objects from the holder's pool (the connect's idempotency guard) and make the holder's own datasource read-only to the admin door — the refusal makes the spec's own invariant (one holder per datasource name; code names are read-only) real at the consumer rather than taking a capability away. `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with `details.datasource` matches the door's existing refusal shape (namespace/base conflict). Holds.
- **The shared helper**: one path for boot and install with three explicit `installed` deltas (names contributed now, fail-fast reported not thrown, withdraw-before-register + uninstall cleanup) is the right altitude; the boot path keeps its exact behaviour and the install path reuses the connection service's retained verdicts rather than inventing a status. The `owned` thunk preserves `AppPlugin`'s "ownership resolution inside the lenient catch" invariant. Holds.
- **Public surface**: the 4 exported types are the helper's parameter/return types, needed for a typed cross-package call; nothing else is exported. The `datasources` member is the minimal answer a CLI/agent needs to see a failed credential at install time without a second call. Holds.
- **Clients (Q7)**: `ui/.../marketplaceApi.ts` types the managed answer as an open TS interface (an added optional member is additive); CLI `os package install` handles unknown non-ok statuses with the generic `printError` of the body's `error.message` (the 409 reads as a named refusal); no spec Zod schema for the install-local answer exists to strict-parse it. Nothing breaks.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-aercb9`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia (seat subagent)`

**VERDICT: PASS**
